CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY
GENOMIC MICROARRAY ANALYSIS REPORT

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Products of conception/placental material
Date Collected: [redacted]
Date Received: [redacted]
Date Reported: [redacted]

REFERRING PHYSICIAN
Dr. [redacted name]
[redacted location]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Fetal loss investigation

TEST PERFORMED
Array Comparative Genomic Hybridization (Array CGH)
QF-PCR for aneuploidy screening

METHODOLOGY
Array CGH analysis was performed using oligonucleotide arrays containing approximately 60,000 probes distributed across the genome. Testing was conducted on the GenomeArray 3000 platform with a median resolution of 120kb. DNA was extracted from products of conception/placental material and hybridized against reference DNA. Data analysis was performed using GenomeScan software with reference to the GRCh37/hg19 human genome assembly.

Quantitative Fluorescence-Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) analysis was performed to screen for common aneuploidies and to exclude triploidy.

RESULT: ABNORMAL

Array CGH Result:
arr[GRCh37] (8)x3

Complete trisomy of chromosome 8 detected

QF-PCR Result:
- Negative for triploidy
- Male chromosome complement (XY)
- Consistent with trisomy 8

No other fully penetrant pathogenic copy number imbalances were identified.

INTERPRETATION
This analysis reveals complete trisomy of chromosome 8 in the submitted products of conception. Trisomy 8 is a chromosomal abnormality that is typically incompatible with fetal survival and is a recognized cause of pregnancy loss. This finding is most likely causative for the fetal loss in this case.

Complete trisomy 8 in pregnancy tissue is most commonly due to a sporadic meiotic or early mitotic error (de novo aneuploidy event). The recurrence risk for sporadic aneuploidy is generally low, estimated at approximately 1% above the maternal age-related risk.

While this finding is most consistent with a sporadic event, a parental chromosome rearrangement involving chromosome 8 has not been completely excluded. If clinically indicated for reassurance purposes, parental blood samples would be accepted for karyotype analysis to rule out a balanced rearrangement.

LIMITATIONS
- Array CGH cannot detect balanced chromosomal rearrangements, polyploidy, or low-level mosaicism (<20-30%)
- The resolution of this array is approximately 120kb; smaller copy number variants may not be detected
- Maternal cell contamination cannot be completely excluded

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss these results and recurrence risks
2. Parental chromosome analysis may be considered if appropriate for reassurance, though the likelihood of identifying a predisposing rearrangement is low
3. For future pregnancies, prenatal diagnosis options should be discussed

This report has been reviewed and electronically signed by:
[redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Director, Cytogenetics Laboratory
[redacted date]
